title: Microsoft 365 admin center: authoritative SharePoint sites for Copilot Search
summary: The briefing passes: the management paths, command, limits and rollout facts are supported, and the documentation gaps are appropriately qualified. A minor licensing clarification should report that the cmdlet reference describes a licensed administrator, while the prerequisites say the licensed user need not be an administrator.

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative-sites page states that a Microsoft Copilot licence is required and links to SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites.
claims.quote: Licensing: A Microsoft Copilot license is required. (See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.)

claims.claim: The feature is included within the Microsoft Copilot licensing entitlement described by its linked prerequisites.
claims.quote: If your organization has at least one Microsoft Copilot license assigned to a user, your SharePoint administrators automatically receive access to SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities to support your Copilot deployment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The prerequisites grant Copilot-supporting SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities when at least one organisation user has a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: At least one user in your organization is assigned a Microsoft Copilot license. (The user doesn't need to be a SharePoint administrator.)
claims.fix: After the tenant-level licensing statement, add: "The Set-SPOSite reference instead describes marking a site as an operation by 'an admin with a Copilot license', while the SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites say the licensed user need not be a SharePoint administrator." Link that sentence to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-sposite?view=sharepoint-ps#-isauthoritative. The two cited Microsoft pages differ on who holds the licence; retain both accounts rather than silently choosing one.
